bibliographic.title: Large language models in real-world clinical workflows: a systematic review of applications and implementation
bibliographic.authors: Yaara Artsi, Vera Sorin, Benjamin S. Glicksberg, Panagiotis Korfiatis, Girish N. Nadkarni, Eyal Klang
bibliographic.citation_apa: Artsi, Y., Sorin, V., Glicksberg, B. S., Korfiatis, P., Nadkarni, G. N., & Klang, E. (2025). Large language models in real-world clinical workflows: a systematic review of applications and implementation. Frontiers in Digital Health, 7, 1659134. https://doi.org/10.3389/fdgth.2025.1659134

methodology.method_family: systematic review with PROBAST risk-of-bias assessment
methodology.sample_description: Peer-reviewed, full-text, English empirical studies reporting real-world LLM implementation in clinical settings; four studies published 2024–2025, all using GPTs
methodology.technology_context: GPT-based LLMs deployed in clinical workflows for outpatient communication, mental health support, inbox message drafting, and clinical data extraction

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article is a peer-reviewed systematic review of real-world LLM implementation in clinical workflows within regulated healthcare. It is relevant to the review scope via deployment challenges, human oversight, regulatory delays, and communication-oriented use cases, but its primary focus is clinical applications and implementation outcomes rather than conversational governance frameworks, guardrails, auditability, or accountability mechanisms for conversational AI.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and early methods/results pages were provided; full synthesis, governance-specific findings, and detailed appraisal require full-text verification.

appraisal.notes: PROSPERO-registered systematic review with predefined databases, inclusion criteria, dual independent screening, and PROBAST quality assessment. The included evidence base is very small (n=4). Provided text supports methodological transparency but does not show full data extraction, synthesis, or discussion of governance mechanisms in depth.

cerqual.explanation: The review appears methodologically sound for its stated aim, but confidence is moderated by the very limited number of included real-world studies and because only partial text was available to assess full thematic coherence and adequacy of evidence on governance-related claims.

coding.theme: Real-world LLM implementation in clinical workflows
coding.subtheme: Implementation benefits and systemic governance barriers

synthesis.main_claim: Early evidence suggests LLMs can enhance clinical workflows, but real-world adoption remains constrained by systemic, technical, and regulatory barriers, including lack of post-deployment monitoring.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a focused systematic synthesis of four real-world clinical LLM implementation studies, reporting use cases, outcomes, and implementation challenges in regulated healthcare settings.
synthesis.limitations: Very small included corpus (four studies); challenges include performance variability, limited generalizability, regulatory delays, and lack of post-deployment monitoring; full-text governance analysis not visible in provided excerpt.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on real-world regulated healthcare LLM deployment, especially for communication-related use cases and for barriers involving oversight, monitoring, regulation, and safety/risk.

evidence.claim: Article is a systematic review of real-world LLM implementation in clinical workflows.
evidence.excerpt: This systematic review aims to evaluate the literature on real-world implementation of LLMs in clinical workflows

evidence.claim: Search covered major databases with empirical clinical implementation focus.
evidence.excerpt: We searched MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar for studies published between January 2015 and April 2025 that assessed LLMs in real-world clinical applications.

evidence.claim: Inclusion required peer-reviewed empirical LLM implementation in clinical settings.
evidence.excerpt: Inclusion criteria were peer-reviewed, full- text studies in English reporting empirical implementation of LLMs in clinical settings.
Study quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PROBAST tool.

evidence.claim: Only four GPT-based real-world studies were included.
evidence.excerpt: Four studies published between 2024 and 2025 met inclusion criteria. All used generative pre-trained transformers (GPTs).

evidence.claim: Reported applications include communication-oriented clinical tasks.
evidence.excerpt: Reported applications included outpatient communication, mental health support, inbox message drafting, and clinical data extraction.

evidence.claim: Deployment was linked to efficiency and satisfaction benefits.
evidence.excerpt: LLM deployment was associated with improvements in operational efficiency, user satisfaction, and reduced workload.

evidence.claim: Key barriers include regulatory delays and absent post-deployment monitoring.
evidence.excerpt: challenges included performance variability across data types, limitations in generalizability, regulatory delays, and lack of post- deployment monitoring.

evidence.claim: Authors recommend human oversight for safe scalable use.
evidence.excerpt: future efforts should prioritize standardized evaluation metrics, multi-site validation, human oversight, and implementation frameworks tailored to clinical settings.
Systematic Review Registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/ recorddashboard, PROSPERO CRD420251030069.

evidence.claim: Outcomes framework included safety versus risk.
evidence.excerpt: Outcomes encompassed workflow, efficiency, usability, adoption, clinical impact, and safety vs. risk.

evidence.claim: Simulation-only and non-LLM NLP studies were excluded.
evidence.excerpt: We excluded simulation-only studies (including vignette-based evaluations not used to guide real patient care), bench evaluations without deployment, and non-LLM NLP.
